title: Students, Batches and Attendance for Coaching | AllCoaching
description: Split a course's students into batches with their own timetable and attendance register. A batch belongs to one course; the enrolment stays safe.
keywords: batch management for coaching, course vs batch, student attendance app, online attendance register, coaching timetable, morning and evening batch
lede: A course is what you sell: videos, notes and tests. A batch is a group of that course's students who study together on one timetable, with attendance taken. Students buy the course, not the batch, and one course can run many batches.
notes: Only enrolled students can join a batch
Removing a student keeps their course enrolment
card: Morning, evening and weekend batches of one course, with timetable and attendance.

sections.body: When you create a batch, the Course field is what links it to a course, and only that course's students can be added to it. Once the batch is made, its course cannot be changed. One course can have many batches, such as Morning, Evening and Weekend.
bullets: Name, course, first and last class, class days and time
Online, in a classroom, or both; teacher and seats
The timetable is made for you when you press Create batch
Add students lists only those enrolled in the course and not yet in the batch
sections.alt: Create a batch dialog with the batch name, the linked course, class dates, class days and start time

sections.body: On the day of the class, press Take attendance, mark everyone present in one click, change whoever was late or absent, and save the register. Attendance comes from the batch and progress comes from the course, and you see both side by side.
bullets: Present, late or absent for each student
Download the register, and see the last ten classes at a glance
Students tab: attendance beside lessons finished and last active
Timetable: add a topic, cancel a class or add an extra class
sections.alt: Batch attendance register with present, late and absent for each student, and the last ten classes below

sections.body: Remove a student from a batch, or delete the whole batch, and the student is not removed from the course. Their course carries on exactly as before; only that batch's attendance stops counting. The order is always the same: a student takes the course first, then you place them in a batch.
bullets: Removing a student keeps them enrolled in the course
Deleting a batch never touches course enrolments
Fixed batch dates in a course's Settings are only the course's own dates, not a batch
Timetable, students and attendance all live in Batches
sections.alt: Confirmation to remove a student from a batch, stating they stay enrolled in the course

steps.d: Open Batches, press Create batch, give it a name and pick its course.
Choose the first class, class days, time, length, mode and seats.
Tick the course's enrolled students who should study in this batch.
On class day, mark everyone present, change who was late or absent, and save the register.

faq.q: What is the difference between a course and a batch?
faq.a: A course is what you sell: videos, notes and tests. A batch is a group of that course's students who study together on a timetable, with attendance. Students buy the course, not the batch.

faq.q: How do I create a batch for my coaching?
faq.a: In Batches, press Create batch and fill in the name, course, days, time and seats. The timetable is made for you.

faq.q: How do I take student attendance online?
faq.a: Open the batch, press Take attendance, Mark all present, change who was late or absent, and Save register.

faq.q: How do I run morning and evening batches of one course?
faq.a: Create two batches of the same course, like Morning and Evening, and add that course's students to each.

faq.q: If I remove a student from a batch, do they lose the course?
faq.a: No. Removing a student from a batch, or deleting the batch, keeps their course enrolment. Only that batch's attendance stops counting.
